items.item_text: Possession of the education and legal requirements for the practice of medicine in California as determined by the California Board of Medical Quality Assurance.
MD or DO from an accredited institution.
Completion of an accredited psychiatry residency program.
Experience providing care in adult inpatient psychiatry and/or child & adolescent inpatient psychiatry settings.
Board Certification in Psychiatry
Prior leadership experience in inpatient behavioral health, psychiatric service lines, or hospital-based psychiatry programs.
Must meet UC and affiliated hospital credentialing requirements.
Experience in behavioral health inpatient and outpatient settings.
Demonstrated clinical experience in inpatient psychiatry.
Experience in program development, clinical operations, quality improvement, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Board Certification or Board Eligibility in Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
Experience in academic medicine, clinical teaching, and mentorship of learners.

Clinical Leadership and Patient Care: Provide direct inpatient psychiatric care for adult and child/adolescent patients, including assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, medication management, and coordination with interdisciplinary teams. Oversee clinical workflows and support safe, high-quality patient care. (60% time)

Program Development and Medical Direction: Lead the development and implementation of the inpatient psychiatry service line, including clinical protocols, care pathways, operational workflows, and collaboration with hospital and faculty leadership to support program growth and launch readiness. (20% time)

Communication and Care Coordination: Partner with patients, families, guardians, case management, social work, and community providers to support continuity of care, discharge planning, and effective transitions across settings. (10% time)

Teaching and Academic Engagement: Support the academic mission through teaching, mentorship, and participation in educational activities for medical students, residents, and other trainees, as applicable. (10% time)
Possession of the legal requirements for the practice of medicine in California as determined by the California Medical Board.
Maintenance of California Medical License and Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) prescribing number.
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Constantly
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Frequently
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Occasionally

Other: Must be able to lift up to and push / pull 50 pounds. Must be able to assist patients with mobility during rooming patients and in preparation for exams/procedures. Able to respond to assist in emergency scenarios; administer CPR.
Advanced communication and interpersonal skills.
Computer proficiency and first-hand experience in using electronic health records systems to document patient interactions and coordinate care.
Ability to work effectively with staff and patients from diverse ethnic/racial backgrounds, educational levels, sexual orientations and identities.
Ability to stay abreast of new medical knowledge, and to maintain and increase expertise and skills as relevant to clinical practice.
Ability to work independently under general direction and to work collaboratively with others.
